Chapter 8: Giving Back — Creating Opportunities for Others
With every new step she took, her sense of responsibility kept growing. It wasn’t enough just to make it out herself—she felt this deep pull to reach back and help others do the same.
The memories of her own struggles were always close: the hunger, the uncertainty, those moments when even one small act of kindness changed everything. She knew firsthand how much it meant to have someone believe in you, or to have a helping hand when you’re at your lowest.
So, she started searching for ways to give back. At first, it was pretty simple—tutoring students who reminded her of herself, volunteering at the local shelters, organizing food drives in her community. Sure, the work was demanding, but it gave her a sense of purpose that no paycheck ever could. She saw how small acts really add up, how just a few hours of her time could shift the direction of someone else’s life.
As her influence grew, so did her ambitions. She took things further, starting a scholarship fund for girls from her old neighborhood. She was determined to clear at least one barrier from their path. The process? It was slow, with all sorts of bureaucratic hurdles and setbacks she never saw coming. But every time a student got support, every time a family celebrated a new opportunity, she was reminded—this is why it matters.
She didn’t stop there. She became an advocate, using her platform to push for real, lasting change. She met with local leaders, spoke at public forums, wrote op-eds calling for better access to education and resources. It was often frustrating—progress came in fits and starts, and there were days when it felt like nothing would ever change.
But she’d learned something important: real change is rarely quick or easy. It’s built from countless small efforts, each one stacking on the last.
Most people underestimate just how powerful giving back can be. They think you need money, or influence, when really, the most valuable thing you can offer is your time, your attention, your belief in someone else’s potential.
For her, giving back wasn’t just a duty—it was a way to honor the people who’d helped her along the way. And it was her way of making sure the doors she’d walked through stayed open for everyone coming up behind her.
